question.prompt: At a gathering of \(30\) people, there are \(20\) people who all know each other and \(10\) people who know no one. People who know each other hug, and people who do not know each other shake hands. How many handshakes occur?

solutions.title: Count each handshake twice
solutions.explanation:
Add the number of handshakes each person takes part in. This will count every handshake twice, once for each participant.

Each of the \(20\) people who know one another shakes hands with the \(10\) outsiders, contributing \(20\cdot10\) to this count. Each of the \(10\) outsiders shakes hands with all \(29\) other people, contributing \(10\cdot29\).

Thus the actual number of handshakes is
\[
\frac{20\cdot10+10\cdot29}{2}
=\frac{200+290}{2}
=245.
\]
The answer is \(245\), choice **B**.
